page: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EBDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This server includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage for high block storage performance. Benchmark results show average performance across most compute and memory metrics, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance at 31078.76 and a Passmark CPU score of 36975.23. Notably, the memory subsystem demonstrates strong performance, achieving a Passmark memory score in the top 25% tier. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 151.75 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 69.57 GB/sec.

The E32bds_v5 is designed for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and enterprise applications. It achieves 31.6 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 34.04 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. While it performs strongly on small-model LLM text generation at 269.82 tokens per second, it exhibits weaker performance on larger models, such as 6.63 tokens per second for 70B model prompt processing, due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-dense relational databases and caching layers rather than large-scale AI training.
